items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I heard some of those same elements across the street from Miss Mary’s place, out of the juke box.

ctx.x: Did you feel that the gospel and the spiritual tradition really loomed large in your musical . . . ?

Absolutely. Oh yeah, man, the feeling part of it. Gospel music is really, I think, the root – really this music is the root of all music. I did some research on it. It’s really the root of it all. It became in some ways perverted, because music in its purest sense was featured with pure worship. That’s what it was all about, pure worship. But, like many other things become perverted over time, becomes contaminated with other elements. Now, what comes to mind – not to say it’s contamination – but what comes to…
